c1-33-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Reading a Poem
c1-33-01.scenario: A friend has read a poem by a Nyugat poet and asks how you read such a poem.
c1-33-01.prompt: Tell your friend how you read the poem.
cues: Say how you read the poem
c1-33-01.target: A verset többször elolvasva új jelentésrétegeket találunk.
c1-33-01.english: Reading the poem several times, we find new layers of meaning.
c1-33-01.canDo: I can describe how I read a poem with a *-va/-ve* participle (*a verset elolvasva*, *a képeket dekódolva*).

c1-33-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Voices in a Poem
c1-33-02.scenario: Your friend asks why a poem by a Nyugat poet is so hard to sum up.
c1-33-02.prompt: Tell your friend what the voices in the poem do.
cues: Say what they give the poem
c1-33-02.target: Az egymással feleselő hangok kettős jelentést adnak a versnek.
c1-33-02.english: The voices answering one another give the poem a double meaning.
c1-33-02.canDo: I can describe a text with a participle before the noun (*a feszültséget fenntartó kép*, *az egymással feleselő hangok*).

c1-33-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Writer's Duty
c1-33-03.scenario: After a talk about Babits Mihály, your friend asks what a writer should do when an injustice happens.
c1-33-03.prompt: Tell your friend what the writer's duty is.
c1-33-03.target: Az írástudónak kötelessége szólni, ha igazságtalanság történik.
c1-33-03.english: It is the intellectual's duty to speak up when an injustice happens.
c1-33-03.canDo: I can say what a writer's duty is (*az írónak kötelessége kiállni az igazság mellett*).

c1-33-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Effect of a Translation
c1-33-04.scenario: Babits Mihály translated Dante's Divina Commedia. Your friend asks what a critic says about the effect of such a translation.
c1-33-04.prompt: Tell your friend what the critic says.
cues: Say how much the translation changed the language
c1-33-04.target: A kritikus szerint a fordítás számottevően gazdagította a magyar nyelvet.
c1-33-04.english: According to the critic, the translation enriched the Hungarian language considerably.
c1-33-04.canDo: I can say how much a work influenced another (*számottevően*, *szembeötlően*, *jelentősen*).

c1-33-05.title: Communicative Challenge: European Literature as One Whole
c1-33-05.scenario: After the talk about Babits Mihály's book, your friend asks how national literatures belong to European literature.
c1-33-05.prompt: Tell your friend, with a comparison.
cues: Start the comparison with a river
Say what the national literatures do
c1-33-05.target: Ahogyan a folyók a tengerbe ömlenek, úgy egyesül minden nemzeti irodalom az európai kánonban.
c1-33-05.english: As rivers flow into the sea, so every national literature joins the European canon.
c1-33-05.canDo: I can compare two things with *ahogyan … úgy* (*ahogyan a folyók a tengerbe ömlenek, úgy egyesül minden nemzeti irodalom az európai kánonban*).

c1-33-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Learning from Poets
c1-33-consolidation.scenario: Your friend asks what poets and readers have in common.
c1-33-consolidation.prompt: Compare the poets with the readers.
c1-33-consolidation.target: Ahogyan a költők tanultak egymástól, úgy tanulunk mi is a verseikből.
c1-33-consolidation.english: As the poets learned from one another, so we too learn from their poems.
c1-33-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for reading a poem, its voices, a writer's duty and the unity of European literature.
